title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 143 (Guarantee obtained by concealment invalid)

content.overview: Section 143 provides that any guarantee which the creditor has obtained by means of keeping silence as to material circumstances is invalid.
content.glance: A guarantee obtained by the creditor keeping silence as to material circumstances is invalid.
content.study: Any guarantee which the creditor has obtained by means of keeping silence as to material circumstances is invalid. Current-law framing: silence as to material circumstances by the creditor invalidates the guarantee.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Any guarantee which the creditor has obtained by means of keeping silence as to material circumstances is invalid.

examples.title: Silence as to material fact
examples.body: Creditor keeps silent about a material circumstance when obtaining the guarantee. The guarantee is invalid under Section 143.

hypotheticals.question: The creditor conceals a material circumstance known to him when taking the guarantee. Is it valid?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 143 provides that a guarantee obtained by keeping silence as to material circumstances is invalid.
